[AbortedError](./hopgraph.abortederror.md)


</td><td>

The reason on a load's or a dry run's signal when the run aborted it on its own: its deadline passed, or the run failed (`cause` is what failed it). When the caller's own signal aborts, the loads see the caller's reason instead, and the run rejects with it, as `fetch` does.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[CostChangedError](./hopgraph.costchangederror.md)


</td><td>

Gated reads priced again on resume cost more than was approved: nothing of them is billed. `gates` lists every gate the run refused, by gate id, so that they can all be approved again in one round; `gate`<!-- -->, `approved` and `priced` are the first of them.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

</td><td>

The builder, the plan of a run, or `checkGraph` refuses the declared graph.


</td></tr>

Every error the library throws: a stable `code`<!-- -->, and a message that starts with `hopgraph: `  and holds no key, value or source message.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[ValidationError](./hopgraph.validationerror.md)


</td><td>

Base rows the run refused before reading anything. Named by row id and field, never by value:  a schema's own issue messages may quote the value, so they are not kept.

Checks what the compiler cannot, for the application's graph test: every pair of a base in `bases` and a provider has a route; every route's paths chain from its base to its provider's entity; every route starts at a base; every loader is used; every entity whose carried attributes a load or a projection needs has a hydrator. It also lists, per pair, the relation paths of up to `maxDepth` relations (4) that no route uses, for a committed file, so that a new relation that opens a way shows in review.


</td></tr>

</td><td>

A runner over `graph` with what holds for the process: create it once at startup, then `read` or `run` at each call site. An env the run would refuse (caps or limits that are not whole numbers from 1, a health or an inflight object not made by `createHealth` or `createInflight`<!-- -->) is refused here, with a `DefinitionError`<!-- -->, rather than at the first call. Given no cache, the runner keeps the scopes of the gates its runs stop at, and nothing else, so that an approval still covers a part of its keys on resume.

Starts a graph. Type arguments first (no partial inference in TypeScript): `Ctx` is what a run carries (`undefined` for a graph whose runs carry nothing: a run may then leave `ctx` out), `Meta` what every field must say about itself, `Conn` the connector names.

<tr><td>

[run(graph, options)](./hopgraph.run.md)


</td><td>

Reads the requested providers for the base rows along the declared routes. Rejects with a `DefinitionError` before reading anything when the routes cannot run, with the signal's reason when `options.signal` aborts, and with what failed the run when a load throws what rejects it. `options.ctx` is checked against the graph's `Ctx` (`NoInfer`<!-- -->: the graph alone says what it is), and may be left out when that admits `undefined`<!-- -->. A provider with no route from one of the base rows' entities does not compile, when those are literals (`RoutedProviders`<!-- -->). A run given no `cache` keeps nothing, the scopes of its gates included, so an approval covers its own gate id only: a resume whose keys come in parts (some loaded meanwhile by another call) stops at a gate of its own. A runner given no cache keeps those scopes (`createRunner`<!-- -->); else give a cache. A runner (`createRunner`<!-- -->) gives the options that hold for the process once.


</td></tr>

</td><td>

The store the executor reads and writes, per key. An answer's key is `hopgraph:1:answer:<loader id>:<loader version>:<sha256>`<!-- -->, the digest of the key id, the values of the loader's needs and hints, its declared ctx data and the restriction: a load's answer is a function of its key and its needs, and a need may come from the link that reached the ref (a window around the referring track's date), not from the entity. The run also keeps there the scope of a gate it stopped at (`hopgraph:1:gate:<gate id>`<!-- -->, retention `hour`<!-- -->), so an approval covers a part of its keys on resume. The application maps a retention to a duration and owns the store (memory, a key-value server, a framework's data cache).

[KeyInputOf](./hopgraph.keyinputof.md)


</td><td>

What a base row of entity `N` gives as its key: what its key's schema accepts, when the schema  says (`z.string().transform(Number)`<!-- -->: a string); the key type when it says `unknown`<!-- -->, as a  `Schema<T>` does, so that a key is still checked.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[KeyOf](./hopgraph.keyof.md)


</td><td>

The key type of entity `N` among the entities `E` of a graph: what its key's schema parses to,  as loads, links and results see it.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[LinkOut](./hopgraph.linkout.md)


</td><td>

What a projection returns for one target: its key, the link's attributes, and attributes of  the target it already knows (so the target needs no hydration for them).


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[LoaderInput](./hopgraph.loaderinput.md)


</td><td>

What `g.loader()` takes: a loader's declaration, typed by the graph's entities, run values and  connectors. README, "Loaders", walks through it.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[LoadReason](./hopgraph.loadreason.md)


</td><td>

Why a load could not read a key: its source failed it, or the load knows the source is not readable for this caller. The other reasons are the run's to give: a load that claimed one (an approval awaited, a deadline) would stop a fallback at a gate nobody can approve. A run reads any other reason an envelope gives as `failed`<!-- -->.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[NamedFields](./hopgraph.namedfields.md)


</td><td>

What `provider()` returns for rows of type `R`<!-- -->: the provider, or why not, which a route or a run then refuses, for rows with an index signature or a pattern of keys (an index over `x_${string}`<!-- -->): such a key names no field, so `raw` names none of them and the run keeps none, while a result would type every key of the pattern. Checked on the result, not on `raw`<!-- -->: a check on `raw` that reads `R`<!-- -->'s keys makes the compiler stop reading `R` from `project`<!-- -->.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[ProviderRef](./hopgraph.providerref.md)


</td><td>

A provider a run is asked for: its id, or the provider itself, whose rows the result then  types by its fields.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[ProviderResults](./hopgraph.providerresults.md)


</td><td>

Per requested provider, by its id, its result. A provider asked as itself has its own key and typed rows: a key that is always there when the providers are a list written out (a tuple) and that element is one provider, and a key that may be missing when the element may be one of several (`cond ? lines : names`<!-- -->) or the list is an array. A provider asked by id is read by any string, as a field picker reads it, and may be missing.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[RawFields](./hopgraph.rawfields.md)


</td><td>

What a provider's `raw` must be for rows of type `R`<!-- -->: every value a row holds, with its meaning. The run keeps of a row the fields `raw` names, and a result types them as `R` does, so a row type whose fields `raw` cannot name is refused, with why: `any` (what `JSON.parse` returns), and a union of shapes (only the fields they share could be named). The rows are read from `project` alone: the field specs are `NoInfer`<!-- -->. A row type may be an interface or a type alias.

`any` is told by `unknown extends R`<!-- -->, not by the usual `0 extends 1 & R`<!-- -->: the rows are constrained to `object` so that an interface is accepted, and the compiler reduces `1 & R` to `never` for a type parameter constrained to `object`<!-- -->, which would let `any` through.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[ReadCall](./hopgraph.readcall.md)


</td><td>

What `read` takes besides the entity, the keys and the providers: what holds for this call.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[ReadKey](./hopgraph.readkey.md)


</td><td>

One key of entity `N` as `read` takes it: the key, typed by the entity's key schema; or, for an entity that declares `context` attributes (only a base row or a link brings them, never a hydrator), `{ key, carries }` with every one of them, and any other carried attribute the row already knows.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[ReadKeys](./hopgraph.readkeys.md)


</td><td>

The keys `read` takes for entity `N`<!-- -->: one, or a list. A key that may be an array is given in a list, so that one key is never read as several. None for a name that may be one of several entities (`cond ? "track" : "artist"`<!-- -->), whose key type is not one, nor for a graph whose type does not say its entities.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[Ref](./hopgraph.ref.md)


</td><td>

A ref as a load or a projection sees it: the key, the declared needs (present), and the  declared hints (optional: there when the base row or the link brought them, never hydrated,  never a reason to be unknown).


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[Retention](./hopgraph.retention.md)


</td><td>

How long a key's answer is kept: the application maps these to durations (cache port). An  unknown is never kept. `hour`<!-- -->: an answer that cannot change before the source's next load (a  table loaded at night found nothing) but may then.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[RoutedProviders](./hopgraph.routedproviders.md)


</td><td>

The providers `Ps` as the routes `R` let them be asked for base rows of the entities `Bases`<!-- -->: each as it is given, or, for one no route reaches from one of them, why not (<!-- -->\`<!-- -->provider "credits" has no route from "artist"<!-- -->\`<!-- -->), which the compiler shows where it refuses the call. Bases not known (`string`<!-- -->, rows built at run time) ask only that some route reaches the provider; an id not known (`string`<!-- -->, a field picker's) asks nothing. The run refuses what slips through (`HG_NO_ROUTE`<!-- -->) before it reads anything.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[RouteHow](./hopgraph.routehow.md)


</td><td>

How a route from base `B` reaches a provider keyed by `PE`<!-- -->: a path or a union of paths.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[RunCall](./hopgraph.runcall.md)


</td><td>

What holds for one call: the base rows, the providers, the run's values, who reads, how long the caller waits, and the approvals. `ctx` may be left out when the graph's `Ctx` admits `undefined` (a graph built with `hopgraph<undefined, …>()`<!-- -->); otherwise it is required and checked against the graph's `Ctx`<!-- -->. `Rs` is the type of the base rows: when their entities are literals, `run` checks every provider against the graph's routes from each of them. README, "The runner", says why each option is here and not in `RunEnv`<!-- -->.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[RunOptions](./hopgraph.runoptions.md)


</td><td>

What `run` is asked: what holds for the process and what holds for this call, in one object  (README, "Running", gives each option with its default).


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[Schema](./hopgraph.schema.md)


</td><td>

A schema whose parsed value is `T`<!-- -->, whatever it accepts.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[SpanAttributes](./hopgraph.spanattributes.md)


</td><td>

A span's attributes, by name (DESIGN.md §6).


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[SpanValue](./hopgraph.spanvalue.md)


</td><td>

What a span attribute holds: ids, counts, bytes, durations and outcomes, never a key or a  value.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[StandardResult](./hopgraph.standardresult.md)


</td><td>

What a Standard Schema's `validate` returns: the parsed value, or the issues. The run keeps  neither issue messages nor paths, which may quote the value.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[StrategyMaker](./hopgraph.strategymaker.md)


</td><td>

The `s` a relation's `strategies` receives: `s(loader, { needs, hints, coverage, project })`  makes one strategy, its loader keyed by the relation's `from` and its projection typed.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[UnknownReason](./hopgraph.unknownreason.md)


</td><td>

Why a key or a branch was not read: the reason of an `unknown` outcome.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[Unread](./hopgraph.unread.md)


</td><td>

Why a source was not read at all for this viewer or deployment.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[Validation](./hopgraph.validation.md)


</td><td>

`off`<!-- -->: no schema runs. `boundaries`<!-- -->: base rows, links and hydrations. `strict`<!-- -->: also every  envelope a load returns (envelope.ts) and the values a provider projects (providers.ts).


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[Verdict](./hopgraph.verdict.md)


</td><td>

What a verification says of a candidate link: keep it, drop it, or leave it undecided (it  stays, marked ambiguous).


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[VerifyMaker](./hopgraph.verifymaker.md)


</td><td>

The `v` a relation's `verify` receives: `v(loader, decide)` makes the verification, its loader  keyed by the relation's `to` and its rule typed.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
